title: Guarantee parent-before-child ordering in the runtime skeleton representation
description:
## Summary

`SkeletonSnapshot.Capture` iterates bones in input order and never requires or enforces `ParentIndex < ChildIndex` (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Skeleton/SkeletonSnapshot.cs:64-94). `CreatureRig.Build` still requires the parent Transform to already exist when creating a child (ResolveParent throws at CreatureRig.cs:77-83 if the parent was not created first). Because `SkeletonInferrer` orders by ID, a valid hierarchy whose child ID sorts before its parent ID can fail rig construction. The parent-before-child invariant is therefore only implicit, not guaranteed by the skeleton representation.

Source: docs/audits/creaturecreator-latest-main-audit-26-09-05-01-40-00.md, F-02. Re-verified at HEAD 2a89605 (still input-order only; no reorder/topological invariant).

## Scope

- Make parent-before-child ordering an explicit invariant of the skeleton representation.
- Prefer deterministic topological traversal with stable ID tie-breaking, not incidental authoring/ID order or dictionary enumeration.
- Guarantee `ParentIndex < ChildIndex` for the indexed runtime skeleton.
- Do not introduce an animation framework or generic interfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture where a child ID sorts before its parent ID builds the rig successfully (topologically ordered), not by coincidental authoring order.
- The runtime skeleton representation guarantees ParentIndex < ChildIndex deterministically.
- Ordering is stable across identical inputs.

## Validation

- Focused runtime/PlayMode test with child-before-parent fixture proving the rig builds.
- `dotnet build` Runtime + Tests.Runtime pass 0 errors/warnings.
- Existing rig/pose and skeleton suites stay green.

## Findings

- F-02 open at HEAD: SkeletonSnapshot captures input order only; no ParentIndex<ChildIndex enforcement; CreatureRig.ResolveParent still order-dependent.

## Blockers

- None identified. Related to TSK-0073 (CC-069 rig & pose) and downstream animation traversals.

## Next Step

- Add deterministic topological ordering to the snapshot/skeleton contract with stable ID tie-breaking and a child-before-parent regression.
